items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And I had Lee Young on drums... Lee Young was my drummer.

ctx.x: Yeah, I think it's probably the same.
And I had Lee Young on drums, Lester's brother. And I had a fellow named -- we used to call him Mr. Confrey on trombone, I can't think of his last name. And Tyree Glenn on the other trombone.

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: we started jamming... and Eddie Barefield and Don -- and we started jamming in the day time at the union... As a matter of fact, Eddie Barefield made that arrangement for us on 'Christopher Columbus'.

ctx.x: So it was really a good band, and it was a musical education, really. You know, because you're out here and you're getting a chance to play these -- all these, you know, fantastic arrangements that you know, Barefield's been with Cab Calloway, and you know, we hadn't been to New York, and so it was just -- really a trip.

So I think after that, we did get a job, had a couple of jobs, a couple of three one nighters we played together, and I used to do all the singing with the band, you know. Because I was, as I told you earlier, that I was a singer first, and I used to do all the singing with the band, and we played Easter dances, and we played the big thing down in Santa Monica on the pier, what they used to have every year, and ...

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I know that Callender Eddie Barefield did it

ctx.x: No. But I mean everybody in town

that could play at all, you know. I'm sure ... I know that Tyree did it, I know that Don Basas did it, and I know that Callender Eddie Barefield did it; I know Red Calendar did, because Red Callender Calendar is a very good tuba player, you know, and he was in it every year. And as you said, Marshall was in it, Marvin Johnson ...
Do you have a drum strapped on?
